language.name: English
language.string: Configure actuation, Rapid Trigger, remaps, RGB, profiles and the keyboard's hidden diagnostic controls directly through WebHID.
Desktop Chrome or Edge · HTTPS or localhost · no account required
Per-key actuation, RT, independent press/release values and both dead zones.
Keyboard, media, mouse, lighting and internal firmware functions.
Calibration, raw travel, magnetic-axis metadata and advanced-key inspection stay visible.
The keyboard is the source of truth.

The driver reads the current hardware record before editing, preserves firmware-owned fields, writes only staged changes, commits the correct parameter group, and reads important values back. Firmware flashing is intentionally excluded.
Keyboard effects, a unified live preview, per-key overrides, and the light strip.
The firmware reports indexes rather than effect names.
Choose the active slot, then edit its stored color.
Reads the current LED framebuffer about 24 times per second.
Copy color to all strip LEDs
The new name is written directly to the active onboard profile.
These changes will be written to the active onboard profile immediately.
Apply reviews the staged changes, then writes them directly to the keyboard.
Writes each completed edit to the keyboard automatically.
The current working copy for this key.
Device state, current profile, and selected-key summary.
Per-key Hall actuation, Rapid Trigger, dead zones, calibration, and live travel.
Stage assignments across all four firmware layers.
Profiles, USB behavior, polling rate, sleep, and stabilization.
All advanced key modes remain visible, with safe read-only inspection in this basic release.
Feature bitmap, device metadata, protocol surface, and session log.
Project background, credits, links, and other author-written content.
Choose a layer to inspect its assignments on the keyboard.
Choose a layer, then select a physical key to open its keymap.
Choose which layer to inspect or use for a key combination.
Choose the initial actuation point, then optionally add dynamic press and release sensitivity.
Reset and reactuate from movement instead of fixed return points.
Experimental: edit the firmware's normally hidden fixed release distance.
Keeps both RT sensitivity values identical. Turn off to tune them separately.
Ignore unstable movement at the top and bottom of switch travel.
Off writes 0.00 mm to both top and bottom dead-zone fields.
Show the compact gauge beside the keyboard.
Multiple switches remain visible at the same time.
The local catalog could not be loaded.
No switch profiles match this filter.
Try another brand or search term.
No matching key values in this group.
Click any virtual key, or open the catalog directly. The picker keeps keyboard, media, mouse, firmware and lighting values separated.
Continuous values used by this firmware area.
One firmware bit; no left/right variants.
One permanent preview for both firmware lighting areas.
Select LEDs on the four sides
Drag a rectangular marquee over keys. Hold Ctrl while dragging or clicking to toggle the enclosed keys.
Drag a rectangular marquee over any of the four sides. Hold Ctrl to toggle the enclosed LEDs.
Nine firmware behaviors, one consistent configuration workflow. Choose a card to configure it; use the information button for its captured tutorial.
Detected onboard assignments are grouped by action. Removals stay staged until Apply changes.
For a better experience, please recalibrate your keyboard.
Up to four keycodes at multiple press/release points.
Two or three key actions at distinct travel depths.
Tap one function and hold another after a time threshold.
Latch a key action with firmware timing.
Trigger a command when the key rebounds to its set position.
Resolve two opposing keys using one of four captured firmware modes.
Monitor two selected keys and trigger the key pressed farther.
Send an eight-bit modifier mask and one trigger key together.
Record and assign ordered key-down/key-up sequences.
Select one key to inspect or change its mapping.
Choose the initial actuation point, then optionally add dynamic press and release sensitivity.
Select keys to tune them, or start a device-wide Hall calibration from this keyboard panel.
Actuation, Rapid Trigger, and both dead zones are edited together for the selected keys.
The fixed depth that actuates this key in standard mode.
Experimental: edit the firmware's normally hidden fixed release point.
Every assigned feature receives its own color marker on the virtual keyboard.
Trigger paired actions with an end delay.
Compare two keys by travel and prefer the deeper input.
Connect the keyboard to read its onboard advanced records.
The keyboard and all 38 perimeter LEDs stay visible while the settings below change.
Live preview only. Choose the keyboard effect in the controls below.
Controls the main keyboard LED area.
Eight firmware choices. The first entry is the original driver's rainbow palette; the remaining seven are editable RGB colors.
Index 0 is rendered as a moving spectrum by firmware. Its captured seed RGB is red and all hue bytes are 0.
This is a selector value, not an extra editable color or a hidden H-byte flag.
Hardware behavior, onboard profiles, local backups, and the driver's appearance in one quieter workspace.
Firmware-owned operating mode and scan behavior.
Windows = 0 · macOS = 1 in the original protocol.
Changing this restarts the USB interface and reconnects automatically.
Use 0 only if you want the firmware to keep lighting awake.
Firmware key-stability filtering for small magnetic fluctuations.
Rename or switch the loaded configuration.
The quick switch remains at the top of the navigation bar.
Inspired by the token-based light and dark surfaces found in the ATK Hub capture. Stored only in this browser.
Keep a local JSON copy independent of the manufacturer cloud.
Potentially destructive device operations remain deliberately guarded.
Visible for completeness, disabled until a physical-device restore packet is captured and verified.
Hidden generic features remain visible even when their bit is off.
Firmware upgrade and bootloader commands are intentionally absent.
Place up to four key values across one complete press-and-release lifecycle.
The original AE64 DKS editor uses a fixed 0.1–3.3 mm threshold range.
Toggle the original P1–S–P2–S–R2–S–R1 cells. Dragging is an optional shortcut for painting adjacent cells.
The seven visible cells map to each action’s captured 8-bit mask. The center S cell represents both internal turnaround bits, exactly as the original driver writes them.
At least one output key is required. Each lifecycle cell remains independently optional, as in the original editor.
